intro.caption: Lesson 3-4 — graphing ratio tables. Lin spotted a maintenance tunnel on the city grid. Every checkpoint must follow the exact ratio of 1 block east (x) to 2 blocks north (y) — or the kart hits a wall.

balloons.t: This tunnel cuts across the city! Every checkpoint is 1 east to 2 north.
A secret shortcut! I am already narrating the dramatic tunnel exit!
For 2 east and 4 north, I plotted (4, 2)! Looks great!
You swapped x and y! East (x) comes first, north (y) second: (2, 4).

pages.caption: An ordered pair (x, y) puts the x-value (east) first and the y-value (north) second. Swapping them puts you off the route.

balloons.t: Plot our first two checkpoints on the grid: right x, then up y.
The checkpoints make a straight line! What about that extra dot off to the side?
If a dot is off the straight line, it is NOT an equivalent ratio. Avoid it!
The tunnel goes past our table! We need the checkpoints at 7 east and 18 north.
Keep the 1:2 pattern going along the straight line!
Race control needs the exit ramp plotted: 2 blocks east for every 3 blocks north.
Plot it, extend it, and file the route!
Straight through the origin and out into first place! What a line!

win.caption: Equivalent ratios plot as points on a straight line passing through the origin (0, 0).

gates.title: Gate 1 · Plot the Pairs
gates.prompt: Plot the checkpoints for 1 block east (x) to 2 blocks north (y), and name the starting corner.
hints: Conceptual: in (x, y), the first number moves right along the x-axis and the second moves up along the y-axis.
Procedural: start at (0, 0), go right x spaces, then go up y spaces.

steps: For 1 east, north is 3 → plot (1, 3): right 1, up 3.
For 2 east, north is 6 → plot (2, 6): right 2, up 6.
worked.q: What ordered pair shows 4 east and 12 north?

items.q: Plot the two checkpoints for 1 east : 2 north: (1, 2) and (3, 6).

fb.msg: Careful! (2, 1) swaps x and y. Go right 1, up 2 for (1, 2).
Careful! (6, 3) swaps x and y. Go right 3, up 6 for (3, 6).

items.fbDefault: Go right x blocks first, then up y blocks: plot both (1, 2) and (3, 6).

items.q: At 0 blocks east, how many blocks north is the kart, and what is that point called?

options.fb: (1, 2) is the unit-rate point. The origin is where both values are zero.
If you go 0 blocks east, you go 0 blocks north, not 2.

gates.pass: Checkpoints (1, 2), (3, 6), and the origin (0, 0) are locked in.

gates.title: Gate 2 · Read the Line
gates.prompt: Check which points sit ON the 1 east : 2 north line.
hints: Conceptual: every point on a proportional line keeps the exact same ratio y ÷ x.
Procedural: multiply the x-value by 2 to see if it matches the y-value.

steps: Test (2, 6): 2 × 3 = 6, so (2, 6) is ON the line.
Test (2, 5): 2 × 3 = 6 ≠ 5, so (2, 5) is OFF the line.

3 × 2 = 6, not 5. That point sits off the line.

gates.pass: (4, 8) and (5, 10) line up straight from the origin!

gates.prompt: Extend the 1 east : 2 north straight line past the table.
hints: Conceptual: a proportional line continues at the same rate forever.
Procedural: multiply x by 2 to find y, or divide y by 2 to find x.

gates.title: Boss Gate · File the Route
gates.prompt: Plot and extend the 2 east : 3 north exit ramp, and verify why it starts at the origin.
hints: Conceptual: proportional points form a straight line through (0, 0) because 0 of one means 0 of the other.
Procedural: plot (x, y) with east first, north second; scale both by the same factor to extend.

worked.q: For a 3:5 ramp, what is y when x = 12?

items.q: Plot the first two checkpoints for 2 east : 3 north: (2, 3) and (4, 6).

fb.msg: Swapped! (3, 2) puts north first. Plot (2, 3): right 2, up 3.
Swapped! (6, 4) puts north first. Plot (4, 6): right 4, up 6.

items.fbDefault: Plot (2, 3) and (4, 6): east is x (right), north is y (up).

items.q: Why must a proportional shortcut graph pass through (0, 0)?

options.t: Because 0 east means 0 north — both quantities start at zero together
Because every math graph starts at (1, 1)
options.fb: Proportional graphs pass through the origin (0, 0), not (1, 1).

options.t: Because (0, 0) is the highest point on the grid
options.fb: (0, 0) is the starting corner where the axes meet.

gates.pass: ROUTE FILED! Every point lines up straight from (0, 0) to the exit.

journal.heading: Lesson 3-4 — what the secret shortcut taught us
rows: x goes right (east) first, y goes up (north) second. (2, 4) is not (4, 2).
Every proportional ratio graph starts at (0, 0), where both amounts are zero.
Equivalent ratios always line up in a straight line through the origin.
Use the line's rule (like y = 2x) to predict points beyond your table.
journal.quote: "Swapping x and y is a great way to park in a wall." — Lin

teacher.suggested: Use during or after lesson 3-4 (Determine Equivalent Ratios Using Graphs) as one focused read. Whole-class on a projector, pairs on devices, or independent practice. Covers ordered pairs (x, y), plotting ratio tables, proportional straight lines through the origin, and extending patterns.
standards: Make tables of equivalent ratios relating quantities with whole-number measurements, find missing values in the tables, and plot the pairs of values on the coordinate plane
